summary: Iteration 2 testing of Emergent Upsell CRM (booking driver + multi-currency + new team). 28/28 backend pytest cases passed including new tests for: NEW team (Diyea admin + Aryan/Deepin/Vinay/Brian agents) logins, /api/meta booking_drivers list, meeting creation with booking_driver + ?driver= filter, /api/settings GET (both roles) + PUT (admin only, agent 403), Stripe USD preset (upsell_scale=$2500, amount_usd=2500), INR custom payment link with FX conversion (8500 INR / 85 = $100 amount_usd), Razorpay simulate -> lead Won + dashboard revenue (USD) delta exactly equals amount_usd, dashboard booking_drivers widget with meetings/completed/won counts, audit log contains update_fx_rate. Frontend Playwright verified: Diyea admin login + dashboard 'What's Driving Bookings' widget (4 driver-row-* present), Team page lists all 5 members, Meetings page 'Driver' column with hook badges + driver-filter, FX card admin edit + save (toast 'Conversion rate updated'), Payments page renders ₹ symbol + '≈ $' USD equivalents with USD totals ($1,200 collected / $2,700 pending), Aryan agent login hides Campaigns/Team/Audit nav links and FX input absent (read-only).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py remains a single ~880-line file — still works but flagged for modularisation as the app grows (routers per resource).
GET /api/settings is open to agents (correct) but the PUT correctly admin-gates via require_admin — verified.
amount_usd conversion uses get_inr_rate() at creation time and is stored on each payment record, so historical payments stay correct if the rate changes later — good design.
Dashboard sums amount_usd with fallback to amount (legacy rows). Acceptable since freshly seeded DB has amount_usd on every record.
/api/payments/link rounds amount_usd to 2 dp via round(amount/fx_rate, 2) — verified 8500/85=100.0 exactly and 17000/85=200.0 in tests.
Stripe webhook still publicly mounted (no auth dep) — correct, relies on Stripe-Signature verification inside emergentintegrations.
CORS allow_origins default '*' with allow_credentials=True — would be rejected by browsers in credentialed mode; restrict via CORS_ORIGINS in prod (carry-over from iter1).
List endpoints still unpaginated (leads 2000, meetings 1000, payments 1000) — fine for MVP scale.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all critical flows verified visually; one Playwright meet-datetime fill timed out on the specific lead clicked, but booking-driver capture + render are independently proven by backend tests and the Meetings page UI screenshot showing Discount/Support hook badges from earlier API-created meetings)

rca of the issue: N/A — no critical defects found. Booking driver attribution, FX rate persistence, multi-currency payment conversion, USD revenue rollup, and role-scoped access all pass backend assertions and UI verification.
